citation.title: HPG-Diff: Hierarchical physics-guided diffusion with differentiable connectivity constraints for topology optimization
citation.authors: Jinbo Yang, Mingyue Yuan, Boyuan Zhang, Yoshifumi Kitamura, Shikai Jing
citation.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.LG; the manuscript header names Applied Soft Computing). Version of record: Applied Soft Computing 202 (2026) 115899, doi 10.1016/j.asoc.2026.115899 (Crossref, same title and authors). Not open access per Crossref licence metadata; ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403; not accessed
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (8 Jul 2026; only version), full HTML text including Appendices A-G read from https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07233

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screened I-UNCLEAR; the abstract's quantitative classical comparison is compliance error against SIMP reference designs; a SIMP timing appears only in the Sec. 4.7.2 discussion)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Against SIMP-optimized reference designs, HPG-Diff outputs have mean compliance error of 0.87% on 1,800 in-distribution and 5.29% on 1,000 out-of-distribution test problems, with floating material in 2.90% and 2.44% of samples.
claim.key_phrase: achieves average compliance errors of 0.87% (in-distribution) and 5.29% (out-of-distribution)
claim.location: Abstract (sentence 7); numbers in Sec. 4.4.2-4.4.3, Tables 2-3. §5.1 rule 1: the abstract's only quantitative comparison involving the classical method is compliance error against the SIMP references (the same convention as P00375)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not applicable to the quality-stratum primary outcome. Alternative (Table 8, Sec. 4.7.2): SIMP 23.93 s on a multi-core CPU vs HPG-Diff 10.74 s on a single GPU at 64×64 gives 2.23 [derived]; the text calls HPG-Diff about twice as fast as SIMP.
claim.alternatives: (1) Sec. 4.7.2 and Table 8 (speed): 10.74 s (one FEA plus feature calculation 5.92 s, sampling 4.82 s) vs 23.93 s for SIMP, 2.23× [derived]; stratum speed if chosen. (2) Sec. 4.6 case studies vs SIMP ground truth: shelf bracket 4.9962, 5.0398 and 5.0772 vs 5.0506; LoRA 60×20 cantilever 179.1958 and 185.5106 vs 182.8988; bridge 12.9581 and 12.9663 vs 13.0730. (3) Table 7: LoRA-adapted 60×20 model on 200 held-out samples, CE 2.86%, median 0.58%, VFE 1.54%, FM 3.17%. (4) ML-only comparisons: Tables 2-3 vs TopologyGAN, TopoDiff-Guided and DOM; Table 4 vs DOM plus 5 or 10 SIMP steps; Appendix G vs NITO and OAT.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP minimum-compliance optimization: reference designs of the TopoDiff dataset of Mazé et al. [31] (Sec. 4.1); SIMP also timed in Table 8 and used for the case-study ground truths (Sec. 4.6); 5- or 10-step SIMP post-processing inside the DOM baseline (Table 4)
baseline.implementation: not stated (dataset taken from ref. [31]; the SIMP code behind Table 8 and the case studies is not named)
baseline.hardware_classical: a multi-core CPU, model not stated (Table 8 caption)
baseline.hardware_ml: one NVIDIA A100 for training and inference (Sec. 4.3); Table 8 ML timings on a single GPU
baseline.problem_size: 64×64 elements (Table 8 caption; Sec. 4.7.3) [≈8.5×10³ DOFs, derived]; LoRA adaptation at 60×20 (Sec. 4.6)
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated for the reference dataset. The Table 8 caption says 100 steps without saying whether this counts SIMP iterations or diffusion sampling steps. Table 4 SIMP post-processing uses 5 or 10 iterations
baseline.classical_time: 23.93 s per 64×64 problem on a multi-core CPU (Table 8; entered in the post-process column); number of timed problems not stated
baseline.ml_time: 10.74 s per 64×64 problem on a single GPU: 5.92 s for one FEA plus physics-feature calculation and 4.82 s sampling (Table 8)
baseline.training_time: not stated; about 200 epochs, batch 64, AdamW, learning rate 1e-4, 1000 diffusion steps, cosine schedule, one A100 (Sec. 4.3); LoRA fine-tuning time not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; 30,000 SIMP training samples from ref. [31], supplemented with displacement and principal-stress-line fields (Sec. 4.1); LoRA set of 1,000 samples at 60×20 generated by conventional TO (Sec. 4.6, 4.7.3) plus a 200-sample evaluation set
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance error (CE) relative to the SIMP reference, volume-fraction error (VFE) and floating-material share (FM), all on binarized outputs (threshold 0.5) with a standard FEA solver (Sec. 4.2); tail statistics of CE (App. E)
baseline.quality_gap: Test 1 (in-distribution, 1,800): mean CE 0.87%, median 0.16%, VFE 1.38%, FM 2.90% (Table 2). Test 2 (out-of-distribution, 1,000): 5.29%, 0.61%, 1.45%, 2.44% (Table 3); CE standard deviation 31.76%, maximum 791.07%, 2.70% of samples above 30% CE (Table 15). Five inference seeds: mean CE 0.92 ± 0.08% and 6.39 ± 1.33% (Table 14). Some case-study designs have lower compliance than their SIMP ground truth by up to about 2% [derived from Sec. 4.6]

R1.evidence: Sec. 4.1-4.2, Tables 2-3: each binarized output is compared with the SIMP reference for the same boundary conditions and prescribed volume fraction, but volume is only approximately matched (mean VFE 1.38% in-distribution and 1.45% out-of-distribution). The references' SIMP settings and stopping rule are not stated in this article (dataset of ref. [31]). No compute budget is matched; the quality claim does not rely on one.

R2.evidence: Quality stratum: judged on the competence of the SIMP references. Their settings are not stated (ref. [31]); median CE of 0.16% (Table 2) shows the references are usually slightly better than the generated designs, and the few case-study designs that beat SIMP by 0.8-2.0% [derived] (Sec. 4.6) are consistent with local optima, not an incompetent baseline [inferred]. Unsure, so pass.

R3.evidence: Primary outcome is quality only. For C3: training time is not reported (about 200 epochs on one A100, Sec. 4.3); the cost of the 30,000 SIMP training samples, the added displacement and principal-stress-line fields, and the 1,000-sample LoRA set is not reported (Sec. 4.1, 4.6); no break-even.

R4.evidence: Sec. 4.2: all metrics are computed on binarized outputs with a standard FEA solver over all 1,800 and 1,000 test samples (Tables 2-3). Volume error and floating-material share are reported; App. E counts failures (2.70% of Test 2 samples above 30% CE, maximum 791.07%), which shows the averages include outliers [inferred]; App. D repeats inference over five seeds. Case-study figures show selected designs, but the quantitative results cover full test sets.

reporting.n_test_cases: Test 1: 1,800 in-distribution; Test 2: 1,000 out-of-distribution with 5 unseen boundary conditions (Sec. 4.1); 200-sample 60×20 LoRA evaluation set (Table 7); 3 case studies (Sec. 4.6)

notes: Screening code was I-UNCLEAR. Stratum Q follows §5.1 rule 1 and the P00375 convention that compliance error against SIMP references is a quantitative classical comparison; the abstract and conclusion stress CE, floating material and generalization, and mention speed only in general terms. If the verifier instead takes the Table 8 timing as primary (rule 4 or because CE is read as an accuracy metric), the pre-coded speed-stratum verdicts are: claimed speed-up 2.23 [derived]; R1 fail (R1-unmatched: 10.74 s vs a SIMP run on a 64×64 problem while outputs carry 0.87%/5.29% mean CE and 2.90%/2.44% floating material; partial if the CE is read as the method's reported error); R2 partial (R2-hardware-unjustified: single GPU vs multi-core CPU, SIMP code and iteration count unstated; (c) does not apply below 10^5 DOFs; pointer only: if the caption's 100 steps were SIMP iterations, 0.239 s per iteration at 64² would be about 21-53× the project's provisional CPU PARDISO per-iteration medians of 0.0045-0.0116 s [derived], cross-hardware, figures/data/baseline_timings.csv); R3 fail (no training or data cost); R4 pass. Internal observations: Table 8 enters the SIMP time in the post-process column; the Table 2 reference values for TopologyGAN and TopoDiff-Guided appear to be copied from earlier papers rather than rerun [inferred], and P00235's Table 3 labels the same 0.83 value for TopoDiff as a share above 30% CE, whereas this article labels it median CE [which label is right is unverified]. Reporting locators: OOD = Test 2 (Sec. 4.1, Table 3); seeds = App. D; failure = FM columns and App. E; timing = Table 8 caption plus Sec. 4.3 (CPU model, warm-up and repeats not stated); data = Data availability section (on request); no code statement in the article or on the arXiv abstract page. retest_candidate false: no public code, and the primary outcome is quality only.
